parsed.explanation: Rated as one combined regime. Visitors face universal exposure at entry: passport marker rules, refusal of mismatched applicants, and a fraud ground that can bar them for life. Documented custody harms include sexual abuse and forced labour in immigration detention, and corrections policy for trans inmates has been adopted nationally. Within the division, a restroom ban in government buildings has produced a documented arrest and 24-hour detention. A public complaint form lets anyone report trans people in privacy spaces, and the documentary defence is unavailable to visitors. Recourse exists: the hate-crime statute covers gender identity, courts have enjoined some orders, and sodomy law is repealed. These do not offset the documented enforcement of hostile rules. No trans-specific violence data was found, and imprisonment or execution is not documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport markers are fixed to birth sex for new applications. Mismatched applicants are refused and asked for more evidence. Fraud findings can carry lifetime ineligibility. Passports have been confiscated or blocked, leaving some travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry. A national civil-liberties suit is pending, and the policy is challenged in court.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-issued documents that conflict with appearance trigger refusal and discretionary fraud review at the border. Litigation status changes the risk at the moment of travel.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: A visitor who is arrested under the division's restroom trespass provision is held for 24 hours and handcuffed. Immigration custody has documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. National corrections policy from 2026 mandates conversion-style measures, and reporting on trans prisoners was stopped.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: The trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to leave when asked, so it is not automatic arrest on entry. Pretrial release was granted in the documented case.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility rules are enforced through national and division agencies. A documents or facilities dispute can move a traveller from border screening into custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: The division bars trans people from restrooms and locker rooms in public schools and government-owned buildings. It bans transgender pride flags, with $500 a day fines. Dormitory placement is restricted at public universities. Private settings are outside the division's bathroom rule.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses, hotels and gyms are outside the division's facilities ban. The restroom ban applies only to government-owned settings.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National funding and enforcement rules are stacked on the division's restroom ban. The ban's reach into government buildings is paired with a complaint form that invites reports of trans people.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors is banned in the division. Adults may be able to obtain care. National proposed rules and subpoenas of hospital records for under-19s raise exposure for minors. Care access for visiting adults is not documented as restricted.
care_services.protection: Clinicians may treat patients under 25 for their own care. Adult care is not restricted in the division.
care_services.interaction: The care ban applies to minors and so affects travelling families. Care exposure for adults depends on the national funding and insurance framework.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names radically pro-transgender groups as a target. A December 2025 memorandum uses 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist markers. Federal instructions direct prosecution of teachers for social transition support.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy says counterterrorism powers will not target people who simply disagree. Several executive orders have been blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing at national level can shape how police and prosecutors handle trans people encountered in public. Court injunctions limit some of this.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minors face a ban on gender-affirming care in the division. Schools are subject to a complaint regime on restroom use. Parents may face national prosecution risk for supporting social transition in schools. Travelling minors may be refused entry or placed in facilities by sex assigned at birth.
minors_guardians.protection: Conversion therapy on minors is banned in the division, with exemptions for some clergy and parents. Parental and guardian rights are not documented as restricted beyond schools and care.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor travelling with a guardian may be affected by documents at entry, school and facility rules, and care restrictions. The guardian can be exposed to the same complaint and prosecution risks.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific data on violence against trans people was found. Public complaint channels against trans people in privacy spaces are documented. Police-led enforcement of the restroom ban is documented in one case.
street_violence_police_response.protection: The hate-crime statute covers gender identity with enhanced penalties and requires statistics. Sodomy law has been repealed.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Public complaints can prompt police or administrative action against visitors using government restrooms. Hate-crime protection covers street violence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Complaints under the facilities law are not documented with outcome data. Visitors cannot meet the documentary defence with out-of-state documents. Recourse against entry refusal and fraud findings is not documented as working.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined several national orders. The division's highest court requires sex and name changes for residents. Nondiscrimination protection covers employment and housing but not public accommodations.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Courts check some executive actions, but the record shows enforcement of hostile rules at the border, in custody and in government buildings.

anchor_checks.comparison: The 0.25-C anchor has birth-sex housing with assaults, cross-dressing arrests in administrative buildings, and minimal remedies. This case shows arrests and custody harm, but it has no documented assault pattern in custody placement and has stronger recourse through hate-crime law. It sits above 0.25-C.

The 0.45-D anchor has universal registration and database sharing, with harassment and loss of rooms but no custody harm. This case adds documented custody abuse, arrest for facility use and national threat framing. It sits below 0.45-D.

The 0.55-B anchor has secondary screening, refused entry and administrative penalties, with no custody abuse. This case has documented custody sexual abuse and a facility arrest. Its operative exposure is heavier, so it sits below 0.55-B.

parsed.synthesis: The national entry regime and the division's government-building restroom ban both apply to visitors. The division's restroom ban has an arrest record. Immigration custody has documented sexual abuse and forced labour, and a national corrections policy has been adopted. Complaint channels and a documentary defence the visitor cannot meet make discovery and consequence likely in government settings. Partial recourse is documented: the hate-crime statute, injunctions, sodomy repeal and an adult-care path. None of these operate to offset custody and entry exposure, so the rating sits in the Elevated Risk band.
